name: HELM
description: Operator shell for local AI systems. htop meets aircraft carrier CIC meets AI briefing officer.
keyOutputs: Real-time system monitoring (processes, agents, git, network, security)
Claude Haiku AI briefing layer with auto-heal engine
FM radio player with relay proxy
lessonsLearned: Start with monitoring, add intelligence later. The Winamp chrome aesthetic was a force multiplier for motivation. Renaming from HYDRA to HELM was the right call for clarity.

name: Yennefer
description: Voice assistant with personality. Named after the sorceress. Speaks, listens, and reasons locally.
keyOutputs: Working voice loop: listen -> reason -> speak
ElevenLabs TTS integration with custom voice
lessonsLearned: Voice latency is the killer metric. Local inference + cloud TTS is the right hybrid. Users forgive slow thinking but not slow speaking.

name: Staff of Gandalf
description: Security CLI v0.3.0 with Shire Watch network guardian. 'You shall not pass' for your local machine.
keyOutputs: Multi-category security scanning (network, firewall, ports, processes)
Shire Watch persistent network guardian mode
lessonsLearned: Rust is perfect for security tooling: fast, safe, no runtime. The Tolkien theming made dry security scans actually fun to run.

name: vault-rag
description: Hybrid RAG MCP server for Obsidian vault. Semantic + full-text search over personal knowledge base.
keyOutputs: Hybrid search: Qdrant vectors + Tantivy full-text
MCP protocol integration for Claude Desktop/Code
Deploying to WSL2 for always-on access
lessonsLearned: Hybrid search (semantic + keyword) beats either alone. MCP is the right abstraction for tool-use AI. Tantivy is insanely fast for full-text.

name: Obsidian MCP
description: Custom MCP server for bidirectional Obsidian vault sync with daily breadcrumbs.
keyOutputs: Integration with Claude Desktop and Claude Code
lessonsLearned: MCP servers are lightweight to build but the protocol needs careful error handling. Daily breadcrumbs turned out to be more useful than expected for context continuity.

name: Port Enablement Site
description: Customer enablement site for Port.io licensing workshops at port-licensing.vercel.app.
lessonsLearned: Vercel deploy-on-push is the right workflow for enablement content. Customers prefer interactive over static docs.

name: Port Cheatsheet
description: SSO/RBAC workshop materials and cheatsheets for Port.io customers, hosted on GitHub Pages.
lessonsLearned: Cheatsheets need to be scannable, not comprehensive. One page that people actually use beats ten pages that gather dust.

name: Explorations
description: Visual essays repo: AncientWisdomMap, BoltzmannBrain, SoftwareTheory. Interactive explorations of ideas.
keyOutputs: SoftwareTheory: visual essay on software architecture
lessonsLearned: Visual essays are the best way to learn something deeply. Building the visualization forces you to truly understand the domain.

name: Shadow Board Simulator
description: Board simulation with 181 passing tests. Portfolio piece that proved testing discipline.
lessonsLearned: High test count doesn't equal high value. The tests proved I could write them, but the product itself never found an audience. Good for discipline, not for impact.

name: Deepov
description: Meal planning app. Good idea, never finished. Classic side project entropy.
lessonsLearned: Consumer apps need sustained motivation. Building tools for yourself is easier to sustain than building products for hypothetical users.

name: AEGIS
description: System monitoring dashboard with Python event bus. No frontend. Features ported to HELM.
keyOutputs: Process monitoring logic (later ported to HELM)
Proof of concept for system dashboard
lessonsLearned: A monitoring tool without a frontend is a logging tool nobody reads. The event bus pattern was sound but Python was the wrong choice for a desktop app. Electron won.

name: HIVE
description: Multi-agent tmux orchestration system. Never activated. Too complex for a single operator.
lessonsLearned: Multi-agent orchestration for one person is over-engineering. You don't need a hive mind when you're the only bee.

name: HYDRA Multiplexer
description: WebSocket multiplexer spec for agent coordination. Spec only, never built. The name and vision evolved into HELM.
keyOutputs: Name and concept that became HELM
lessonsLearned: Sometimes the best output of a project is the next project. The multiplexer spec was too abstract, but it crystallized what HELM needed to be: a dashboard, not a router.

name: Command Center v3
description: Agent mesh with 5 workflows. Over-engineered for a single operator.
lessonsLearned: Workflow engines are seductive to build and painful to maintain. A single operator doesn't need a 5-workflow mesh. Keep it simple.

name: Platform Health Engine
description: 4-gauge framework: Adoption, Revenue, Blockers, Product Truth. Framework for customer health scoring, not software.
lessonsLearned: Frameworks that map to real decisions get used. The 4 gauges survived contact with actual customer reviews, which is the real test.

name: EAF v3.1
description: Enterprise Adoption Framework v3.1 with playbooks. Structured approach to enterprise customer onboarding.
lessonsLearned: Adoption frameworks need to be prescriptive enough to follow but flexible enough to adapt. v3 found the balance after v1 and v2 were too rigid.

name: Clawdbot / OpenClaw
description: Slack bot running Claude API for channel summarization. Onboarded but not fully deployed.
lessonsLearned: Slack bots need a champion in the workspace to drive adoption. Technical integration was easy; organizational adoption was the hard part.

name: Yennefer VTube Avatar
description: Live2D avatar pipeline design for Yennefer. Designed but never built.
lessonsLearned: Cool concept, zero execution. Live2D has a steep learning curve and the voice assistant worked fine without a face. Scope creep in its purest form.

name: Memory KG MCP
description: Knowledge graph MCP server using @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory. One test entity since August 2025.
lessonsLearned: A knowledge graph with one entity is just a JSON file with extra steps. Need to either commit to populating it or admit vault-rag does the job better.

name: ccusage
description: Token usage analytics CLI for Claude Code sessions. Tracks spend, sessions, and model breakdown.
keyOutputs: CLI for parsing Claude Code usage logs
Integrated into HELM CC Usage panel
lessonsLearned: Usage tracking changes behavior. Once you can see the spend, you naturally optimize. Simple CLI that solved a real daily need.

name: Real-time Meeting Assistant
description: Real-time meeting transcription and summarization prototype.
lessonsLearned: Real-time audio processing needs dedicated GPU time. Competing with Granola and Otter.ai is a losing battle for a solo builder. Better to integrate than compete.
